# Advanced GitHub configuration

Use this reference for settings and files with GitHub behavior. Inspect the target edition, plan, owner policies and workflow needs before enabling a feature. Keep management access limited to the maintainers and automation that need it.

## Configuration inventory

| Surface | Placement and checks |
| --- | --- |
| Funding | Put supported handles and URLs in .github/FUNDING.yml. Confirm the handles are controlled or approved by the project, preview the Sponsor button where eligible, and verify the target pages. README funding buttons may use the same destinations. |
| Issue forms and routing | Put YAML forms and config.yml in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE. Verify the chooser, contact_links, issue permissions and labels. Disable blank issues only if the available routes cover legitimate reports. |
| Private vulnerability reporting | Enable the feature in repository settings where supported. Customize the private form with .github/VULNERABILITY_REPORT.yml or .yaml, then verify its visibility for a reporter and ownership of notifications. |
| Discussions | Enable Discussions when staffed. Use .github/DISCUSSION_TEMPLATE/ with the category-slug filename for category forms on the default branch. Check category, links and permissions. |
| Ownership | Put CODEOWNERS in .github, root or docs in that precedence order. The last matching pattern wins. Confirm owner write access, case and glob syntax, and evaluate ownership from the PR base branch. Protect the CODEOWNERS file itself where appropriate. Enable required code-owner reviews through rulesets or branch protection if intended. |
| Dependency updates and review | Put .github/dependabot.yml on the default branch. Configure real package ecosystems, manifest directories, schedules, grouping and PR volume. Dependabot version updates, security alerts, and security updates are distinct. Use separately configured credentials for private registries where needed. Run dependency review on PRs where supported. |
| CI and release workflows | Store workflow definitions in .github/workflows/ on the branch or ref required by the trigger. Validate PRs and the default branch. Add a runtime matrix only for supported combinations. Use stable check names before making them required. Test release packaging from a clean checkout before publishing and confirm package/version parity and asset integrity. |
| Reusable automation | Use workflow_call for reusable workflows in .github/workflows. Use a composite action when reusing steps within a job. Organization workflow templates live in workflow-templates/ in the organization’s .github repository and have matching properties metadata. |
| Release notes | Configure .github/release.yml when using GitHub-generated notes. Verify label-based categories, exclusions and the changelog. Protect release tags where needed. Test assets and installation at the published tag. Keep reruns from duplicating or silently replacing a published release. |
| Code scanning and project environments | Choose CodeQL default or advanced setup according to language and coverage. For advanced setup, point the workflow to the optional config file explicitly. Use .devcontainer/devcontainer.json for an intentional Codespaces experience. Test setup and builds on a clean environment. |
| GitHub Pages | Use the supported Pages source or a Pages workflow. Keep public docs and deployment artifacts intentional. Verify the live URL, relative paths, asset URLs and custom-domain settings if applicable. |
| Repository settings | Review default branch, rulesets and required status checks, merge options, environments and approvals, Actions access, private reporting, security settings, and enabled Issues, Discussions, Wiki, Pages or Packages. Use repository templates when consumers need a reproducible starting point. Confirm changes in GitHub rather than assuming a committed file applied them. |
| AI features | Use the paths and scopes in [AI readiness](ai-ready.md). Check any setup workflow, hooks, or MCP tools for actual access and execution requirements. |

## Workflow trust and verification

- Start with read-only workflow token permissions and grant specific write permissions only to jobs that need them. Pin external actions to reviewed full commit SHAs. Prefer short-lived OIDC credentials where supported. Never publish with tokens embedded in files or logs.
- For fork PRs, separate untrusted build/test steps from privileged publishing. Avoid checking out and running untrusted code with secrets or a write token, including in a pull_request_target workflow. Pass untrusted event inputs to scripts as data. Set sensible timeouts and concurrency.
- Validate workflow syntax plus a real positive event. Check paths, branches, permissions and required-check names. Test that protection is compatible with path filters and skipped jobs. Verify releases from the consumer perspective and compare checksums when available.
- Treat administrative changes as separate from file edits. Use only authorized settings, and report branch protection, secret creation, entitlement-dependent features and public rollout separately when unverified.
